difficultyReason: Disjunctive syllogism (A or B; not A; therefore B). Students must formalize the stimulus and distinguish it from conditionals and contrapositives in the distractors. Topic varies across choices to prevent content matching.
stimulus: Either the budget shortfall was caused by increased spending or it was caused by a decline in tax revenue. The auditors confirmed that spending did not increase during the relevant period. Therefore, the budget shortfall was caused by a decline in tax revenue.
questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If the bridge collapsed due to metal fatigue, then it was inspected improperly. The bridge did collapse due to metal fatigue. Therefore, it was inspected improperly.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The patient's symptoms result from either a viral infection or an allergic reaction. Laboratory tests have ruled out any viral infection. Therefore, the symptoms result from an allergic reaction.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Whenever production costs rise, retail prices increase. Retail prices have not increased. Therefore, production costs have not risen.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All volcanic eruptions produce ash deposits or lava flows. The eruption at Mount Crale produced lava flows. Therefore, it produced no ash deposits.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The construction delay was caused by poor planning. Poor planning is always attributable to management failure. Therefore, the construction delay was attributable to management failure.

explanations.correct: The stimulus is a disjunctive syllogism: A or B; not A; therefore B. Choice B has the same structure: viral infection or allergic reaction; not viral infection; therefore allergic reaction. Both premises and conclusion match exactly.
explanations.A: This is modus ponens (A → B; A; therefore B) — a conditional argument, not a disjunctive syllogism. Different structure.
explanations.C: This is modus tollens / contrapositive (A → B; not B; therefore not A). The structure is a denied consequent, not elimination of a disjunct.
explanations.D: This treats an 'or' as exclusive and affirms one disjunct to deny the other — a formal fallacy. The stimulus is valid; this is not structurally parallel.
explanations.E: This is a conditional chain (A → B; B → C; therefore A → C) applied to a particular case — different structure from disjunctive syllogism.

difficultyReason: Modus tollens (contrapositive) stimulus: A → B; not B; therefore not A. Distractors include modus ponens, disjunctive syllogism, and a topic-matching trap. Students must identify the denied consequent structure.
stimulus: If a new drug has been approved by the regulatory agency, then it has passed clinical trials. The drug Veritam has not passed clinical trials. Therefore, Veritam has not been approved by the regulatory agency.
questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All approved medications must meet safety standards. Veritam meets safety standards. Therefore, Veritam is an approved medication.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If a sculpture is displayed in the national gallery, it has been authenticated by an expert. The sculpture known as Blue Form has not been authenticated by any expert. Therefore, Blue Form is not displayed in the national gallery.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Either the building is structurally sound or it must be demolished. The building is not structurally sound. Therefore, it must be demolished.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If a product is certified organic, it was grown without synthetic pesticides. This tomato was grown without synthetic pesticides. Therefore, this tomato is certified organic.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Whenever a law is challenged in court, it receives public scrutiny. This law has received public scrutiny. Therefore, it was challenged in court.

explanations.correct: The stimulus uses modus tollens: displayed → authenticated; not authenticated; therefore not displayed. Choice B mirrors this exactly: gallery → authenticated by expert; not authenticated; therefore not in gallery.
explanations.A: Commits the fallacy of affirming the consequent (all A→B; x is B; therefore x is A). The stimulus is valid modus tollens; this is invalid.
explanations.B: Correct. Modus tollens matching the stimulus perfectly.
explanations.C: Disjunctive syllogism (A or B; not A; therefore B). Different argument form.
explanations.D: Affirms the consequent (certified → no pesticides; no pesticides; therefore certified) — invalid and structurally different.
explanations.E: Also affirms the consequent (challenged → scrutiny; scrutiny; therefore challenged) — invalid fallacy, not parallel to valid modus tollens.

difficultyReason: Universal-to-particular instantiation (All A are B; x is A; therefore x is B). Distractors include a scope-shift trap and a reversed-universal trap. Students must confirm both universality and category membership.
stimulus: Every treaty ratified by the Senate becomes binding international law. The Accord of Lismore was ratified by the Senate. Therefore, the Accord of Lismore is binding international law.
questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in which one of the following is most parallel to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Most volcanic islands have fertile soil due to mineral-rich lava. Kela Island is a volcanic island. Therefore, Kela Island probably has fertile soil.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All peer-reviewed studies are subject to editorial scrutiny. Some nutritional claims are not subject to editorial scrutiny. Therefore, some nutritional claims are not based on peer-reviewed studies.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Every musical composition registered with the copyright office is legally protected. The piece titled Nocturne in F is registered with the copyright office. Therefore, Nocturne in F is legally protected.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All rivers that originate in glaciers carry sediment. The Vorlan River carries sediment. Therefore, the Vorlan River originates in a glacier.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some languages with tonal systems are found in Southeast Asia. Mandarin has a tonal system. Therefore, Mandarin is found in Southeast Asia.

explanations.correct: The stimulus is All A are B; x is A; therefore x is B (universal instantiation). Choice C: All registered works are legally protected; Nocturne in F is registered; therefore it is legally protected. Perfect structural match.
explanations.A: Uses 'most' rather than 'all,' and the conclusion uses 'probably' — both the quantifier strength and conclusion modality differ from the stimulus.
explanations.B: This is a universal syllogism eliminating a class (All A → B; some C are not B; therefore some C are not A) — different structure, more complex.
explanations.D: Affirms the consequent (all glacier-origin → sediment; carries sediment; therefore glacier-origin) — invalid, unlike the valid stimulus.
explanations.E: Uses 'some' instead of 'all' and draws a particular conclusion from a particular premise — different quantifier logic.

difficultyReason: Conditional chain (A → B; B → C; A; therefore C). Distractors share a chain-like surface structure but misorder links or introduce a disjunct. Students must track both the chain and the affirmed antecedent.
stimulus: Whenever a city's population grows rapidly, housing demand outpaces supply. Whenever housing demand outpaces supply, rental prices rise sharply. The population of Denverton is growing rapidly. Therefore, rental prices in Denverton will rise sharply.
questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If soil acidity increases, nitrogen-fixing bacteria die off. If nitrogen-fixing bacteria die off, crop yields decline. The soil acidity in the Farlow Valley has increased. Therefore, crop yields in the Farlow Valley will decline.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Whenever interest rates rise, consumer spending falls. Consumer spending in Westmark has fallen. Therefore, interest rates in Westmark have risen.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If a company loses market share, it either cuts costs or raises prices. Redmont Industries has lost market share. Therefore, Redmont Industries will cut costs or raise prices.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Overfishing leads to ecosystem collapse. Ecosystem collapse leads to loss of biodiversity. Loss of biodiversity leads to species extinction. Overfishing is occurring in the Naral Sea. Therefore, species extinction will occur in the Naral Sea.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If deforestation increases, soil erosion accelerates. Soil erosion is not accelerating in the Pelmore region. Therefore, deforestation is not increasing in the Pelmore region.

explanations.correct: The stimulus is a two-link conditional chain plus affirmed antecedent: A→B; B→C; A; therefore C. Choice A matches exactly: soil acidity → bacteria die; bacteria die → yields decline; acidity increased; therefore yields decline.
explanations.B: This affirms the consequent of a single conditional — a fallacy, and only one premise rather than a two-link chain.
explanations.C: This is a single conditional leading to a disjunctive conclusion (A → B or C) — the stimulus has a two-link chain, not a disjunctive consequent.
explanations.D: Three-link chain (A→B→C→D) rather than two — same family but different premise count, violating the structural match.
explanations.E: Modus tollens on a single conditional (A→B; not B; therefore not A) — denies consequent rather than affirming antecedent through a chain.

difficultyReason: Analogy argument (X and Y share properties P and Q; Y has R; therefore X has R). Distractors use universal instantiation or inductive generalization, which are easy to conflate with analogical reasoning.
stimulus: The Karven Bridge and the Telston Overpass were both built using the same steel alloy and the same suspension design. Engineers have determined that the Telston Overpass is vulnerable to harmonic oscillation failure. Therefore, the Karven Bridge is also vulnerable to harmonic oscillation failure.
questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All languages in the Dravidian family share a subject-object-verb word order. Tamil is a Dravidian language. Therefore, Tamil has subject-object-verb word order.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Novel X and Novel Y were both written in the same era and employ the same unreliable-narrator technique. Novel Y has been found to contain intentional anachronisms. Therefore, Novel X also contains intentional anachronisms.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Medrano Glacier and the Pelso Glacier are both receding. Most glaciers that recede are in regions experiencing elevated temperatures. Therefore, the Medrano Glacier is probably in a region experiencing elevated temperatures.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Either compound A or compound B inhibits the enzyme. Compound A has been shown not to inhibit the enzyme in this sample. Therefore, compound B inhibits the enzyme in this sample.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The Crestwood fire was caused by dry conditions and high winds. Fires caused by dry conditions and high winds spread rapidly. Therefore, the Crestwood fire spread rapidly.

explanations.correct: The stimulus argues by analogy: X and Y share properties P and Q; Y has property R; therefore X has R. Choice B exactly mirrors this: Novel X and Novel Y share era and technique; Novel Y has anachronisms; therefore Novel X does too.
explanations.A: This is universal instantiation (All A are B; x is A; therefore x is B), not an analogy between two particular things sharing stated properties.
explanations.C: Combines a shared property with a probabilistic inference from a majority claim — different structure and uses 'probably,' weakening the conclusion relative to the stimulus.
explanations.D: Disjunctive syllogism (A or B; not A; therefore B) — entirely different argument form.
explanations.E: This is universal instantiation: the fire has properties P and Q; all things with P and Q have R; therefore this fire has R. Not an analogy between two particular objects.

difficultyReason: Contrapositive with a negated antecedent setup: All A that are B are C; x is not C; therefore x is not both A and B. Distractors include a correct-topic but wrong-direction trap and an affirmation trap.
stimulus: Every physician who prescribes off-label medications is required to document the rationale. Dr. Harwell has not documented any rationale. Therefore, Dr. Harwell has not prescribed any off-label medications.
questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in which one of the following is most parallel to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Every contractor who uses substandard materials must pay a penalty. Brisco Construction has paid a penalty. Therefore, Brisco Construction used substandard materials.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every architect who submits a design to the competition must include a cost estimate. Lena Forst did not include a cost estimate. Therefore, Lena Forst did not submit a design to the competition.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Any student who fails two exams is placed on academic probation. Marko has been placed on academic probation. Therefore, Marko failed two exams.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All species listed as endangered receive federal protection. The Borrelia moth is not listed as endangered. Therefore, the Borrelia moth does not receive federal protection.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Every pilot certified for international routes must pass a language proficiency exam. Captain Vasil has passed the language proficiency exam. Therefore, Captain Vasil is certified for international routes.

explanations.correct: The stimulus is modus tollens on a universal: All A→B; x is not B; therefore x is not A. Choice B: all architects who submit → include cost estimate; Forst did not include cost estimate; therefore Forst did not submit. Perfect match.
explanations.A: Affirms the consequent (all users of substandard → penalty; paid penalty; therefore used substandard) — invalid fallacy, unlike the valid stimulus.
explanations.C: Also affirms the consequent (fails two → probation; on probation; therefore failed two) — invalid, structurally different.
explanations.D: This is actually a valid inference but uses 'not A; therefore not B' (denies antecedent) — a different and invalid form. Does not match modus tollens.
explanations.E: Affirms the consequent (certified → passed exam; passed exam; therefore certified) — invalid and structurally distinct.

difficultyReason: Disjunctive syllogism with negated second disjunct (A or B; not B; therefore A). Distractors include negating the first disjunct (which would also yield B — testing whether students track which disjunct is denied) and a conditional trap.
stimulus: The decline in the monarch butterfly population is due either to loss of milkweed habitat or to widespread pesticide exposure. Research has shown that milkweed habitat has actually expanded in recent years. Therefore, the decline is due to widespread pesticide exposure.
questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The server outage was caused either by a hardware malfunction or by a software error. Diagnostics confirmed a hardware malfunction. Therefore, no software error caused the outage.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If the harvest fails, the cooperative will take out loans. The cooperative has not taken out loans. Therefore, the harvest has not failed.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The team's poor performance results either from inadequate training or from low morale. An investigation found no evidence of low morale. Therefore, the poor performance results from inadequate training.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Either the painting is a forgery or it was produced before 1850. The painting was produced before 1850. Therefore, the painting is not a forgery.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rising sea temperatures cause coral bleaching. Coral bleaching has been observed on the Narova Reef. Therefore, sea temperatures near the Narova Reef have been rising.

explanations.correct: The stimulus eliminates one disjunct to conclude the other: A or B; not A (habitat expanded, so loss of habitat is ruled out); therefore B. Choice C: inadequate training or low morale; no low morale; therefore inadequate training. Exact match.
explanations.A: Affirms one disjunct (A or B; A is confirmed) and concludes not B — this treats 'or' as exclusive, which is invalid for standard inclusive disjunction. The stimulus denies a disjunct, not affirms one.
explanations.B: Modus tollens on a single conditional (A→B; not B; therefore not A) — different form.
explanations.D: Same trap as A: affirms one disjunct to deny the other — invalid and structurally different from the stimulus's denial of a disjunct.
explanations.E: Affirms the consequent (temperature rises → bleaching; bleaching observed; therefore temperatures rising) — invalid fallacy, different form.

difficultyReason: Two-premise conditional modus ponens applied to a class claim: All A that are B have C; this thing is A and B; therefore it has C. Distractors include a reversed-universal (C→A) and a topic-match trap on a different form.
stimulus: Any technology that processes personal data and operates across national borders is subject to international privacy regulations. This social media platform processes personal data and operates across national borders. Therefore, this social media platform is subject to international privacy regulations.
questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Any organism that reproduces asexually and lacks a nucleus is classified as a prokaryote. This bacterium reproduces asexually and lacks a nucleus. Therefore, this bacterium is classified as a prokaryote.

choices.label: B
choices.text: This social media platform has been found to violate privacy regulations. Any platform that violates privacy regulations is eventually fined. Therefore, this platform will eventually be fined.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Most technologies operating across national borders face regulatory challenges. This platform operates across national borders. Therefore, this platform probably faces regulatory challenges.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Some data-processing companies are subject to international privacy regulations. This social media company processes data. Therefore, this social media company is subject to international privacy regulations.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Any device subject to international privacy regulations must use end-to-end encryption. This application uses end-to-end encryption. Therefore, this application is subject to international privacy regulations.

explanations.correct: The stimulus is: All things that are [A and B] are C; x is [A and B]; therefore x is C. Choice A: All organisms that [reproduce asexually and lack a nucleus] are prokaryotes; this bacterium [reproduces asexually and lacks a nucleus]; therefore it is a prokaryote. Exact match with two conjunctive conditions.
explanations.B: This is a single-condition modus ponens (violates → fined), not a two-conjunct universal. Also, it shares topic with the stimulus — a content-matching trap.
explanations.C: Uses 'most' instead of 'any/all,' yielding a probabilistic conclusion ('probably') — quantifier and conclusion strength differ from the stimulus.
explanations.D: Uses 'some' as the universal premise, making the inference invalid (some A are C; x is A; therefore x is C is a fallacy). Structurally different.
explanations.E: Affirms the consequent (subject to regulations → encryption; uses encryption; therefore subject to regulations) — invalid fallacy, different structure.

difficultyReason: Argument from elimination using an exhaustive list: A, B, or C must be true; not A; not B; therefore C. Distractors include two-option disjunctions and a modus tollens trap. Students must match the three-option exhaustive structure.
stimulus: The gallery's missing painting was removed by a staff member, a visitor, or a contractor working on the premises. Security footage rules out any staff member, and badge records confirm no contractor was present that day. Therefore, the painting was removed by a visitor.
questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in which one of the following is most parallel to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The signal failure was caused by weather interference or equipment degradation. Tests showed no weather interference. Therefore, the failure was caused by equipment degradation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The delegation will meet in Geneva, Vienna, or Brussels. The Geneva venue is unavailable, and the Vienna venue has been rejected by one party. Therefore, the meeting will be held in Brussels.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If the stock price drops, the company will issue bonds. The company has not issued bonds. Therefore, the stock price has not dropped.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Every ancient coin in the collection was minted in Rome, Athens, or Carthage. This coin was minted in Athens. Therefore, this coin is an ancient coin in the collection.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Either the new policy will reduce costs or it will improve efficiency. The policy has not reduced costs. Therefore, it will improve efficiency.

explanations.correct: The stimulus eliminates two of three exhaustive options to conclude the third: A or B or C; not A; not B; therefore C. Choice B: Geneva, Vienna, or Brussels; not Geneva; not Vienna; therefore Brussels. Three-option exhaustive elimination matches perfectly.
explanations.A: Only two disjuncts (A or B; not A; therefore B) — a standard disjunctive syllogism missing the third option that defines the stimulus's structure.
explanations.C: Modus tollens (A→B; not B; therefore not A) — entirely different form with no disjunction.
explanations.D: Affirms the consequent in a universal (all collection coins are from A/B/C; this is from B; therefore it is a collection coin) — invalid and different structure.
explanations.E: Two-option disjunction, like A — does not match the three-option exhaustive elimination of the stimulus.

difficultyReason: Argument combining a general principle with a comparative particular: If X has more of property P than Y, and Y is sufficient for outcome O, then X also achieves O. Distractors include a premise-count trap and a threshold confusion trap.
stimulus: Any soil with a pH below 5.5 is too acidic to support wheat cultivation. The soil in the northern fields has a pH of 4.8, which is lower than 5.5. Therefore, the northern fields cannot support wheat cultivation.
questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A building requires at least twelve support columns to meet safety codes. The Farnam structure has only nine support columns. Therefore, the Farnam structure does not meet safety codes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most clinical trials require a minimum of one hundred participants to yield statistically valid results. This trial enrolled eighty participants. Therefore, this trial probably did not yield statistically valid results.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If an applicant scores below 70 on the licensing exam, the applicant fails. If the applicant fails, a re-examination is required. Applicant Moro scored 65. Therefore, Moro must undergo re-examination.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Holvane River is too shallow for commercial navigation. The Trest Canal is even shallower than the Holvane River. Therefore, the Trest Canal is also too shallow for commercial navigation.

choices.label: E
choices.text: No wine produced in the Caldera region contains more than 13% alcohol. This bottle is produced in the Caldera region. Therefore, this bottle does not contain more than 13% alcohol.

explanations.correct: The stimulus applies a threshold rule to a particular case: anything below threshold T cannot achieve O; x is below T; therefore x cannot achieve O. Choice A: anything with fewer than 12 columns fails codes; Farnam has 9 (below 12); therefore Farnam fails codes. Exact structural match including the explicit threshold comparison.
explanations.B: Uses 'most' rather than a universal rule, and concludes 'probably' — both the quantifier and the conclusion's modal force differ from the stimulus.
explanations.C: Two-link conditional chain (below 70 → fails; fails → re-exam; scored 65; therefore re-exam) — an extra inferential step not present in the stimulus.
explanations.D: Analogy by comparative degree (X is too Y; Z is even more Y than X; therefore Z is also too Y) — a comparative analogy, not a threshold-rule application to a particular value.
explanations.E: Universal instantiation (no Caldera wine exceeds 13%; this is Caldera wine; therefore it doesn't exceed 13%) — different form: no threshold comparison, just category membership.
